decisions: D16 (PRD-266 §3, Gerard 20 Oct): editors may answer questions and grant or deny tool approvals; viewers may not. The needs_answer push goes to owners, admins and editors, never viewers.

D18–D19 (§3): lock screen Open and Answer on an unlocked phone; Face ID before approve is client-side only; NO server step-up. The lock-screen answer posts the existing POST /api/v1/approval-grants/{id}/answer unchanged: its 422 for an option that was not offered is already on main (api/approval_grants.py:392-396), so this wave builds nothing there.

D20 (§3; decisions.md 20): a question push carries its text and options; every other push is generic ('A ticket is ready for review · #0419'); a per-workspace switch push_redact_questions (default off) sends questions generic too, Open only. Android lock-screen visibility PRIVATE is the app's (PRD-001), not the server's.

D21 (§3; decisions.md 21): a self-hosted server posts to Expo's push service only after the operator agrees ('Send notifications through Expo's push service?'). Gerard's standing decision, not code: Expo 'enhanced push security' stays OFF on the Automatos EAS project, or self-hosted push stops working.

D22 (§3): three push types — Needs an answer, Ready for review (the new review_pending: a ticket enters Review), Auto messaged you (the new auto_message: Auto posts unprompted in a person's thread, and the daily digest). Failures, credit events and every other event stay in-app (FR-7).
D23 (§3): the AI-provider consent sheet's data (ai_providers) is W3's US-017: not this wave.

D24 (§3): the daily digest is Auto's Read, posted as Auto's message in each person's Auto thread at their chosen time (07:00 / 08:00 / 09:00 in the phone's timezone); the auto_message push carries it.
D63 (§3): the app deletes nothing. No account or workspace deletion route in any wave.

§4.4 (Push): push is a notification destination, external for quiet hours (silenced unless severity is urgent or security); services/push/ holds the PushSender protocol, ExpoPushSender (100 messages per request, optional EXPO_PUSH_ACCESS_TOKEN), the payload builder and signer, the fan-out (recipients, membership and role re-checked at send time) and the receipts job (disables DeviceNotRegistered tokens); _insert_in_app returns the notification id so the payload carries it; payload {v: 2, type, workspace_id, notification_id, grant_id?, link_type, link_id, ticket_number?, question?, options?, iat, sig}; the title carries PRD-264 D17's fixed AI badge; sig = HMAC-SHA256 with the device's push_key over the canonical v2 message that covers every payload field but sig, and expires after 7 days (K9; the lead's 21 Oct decision supersedes §4.4's type|grant_id|question|options); preferences accept push rows; a device receives push only when push_enabled and, on a local install, the operator agreed.

§4.5 (Daily digest): a job on the APScheduler host every 15 minutes posts Auto's Read (services/digest_service.py) once per person, workspace and local date when a device's digest_time passes in its timezone, through deliver_background_message; several phones produce one digest.

§4.10 AGENTS.md exception 2 (approved by Gerard 20 Oct; tracking issue #1254; this wave's PR records it): ONE third-party client, services/push/expo.py, against 'integrations go through Composio; no new third-party API clients'. Push is platform infrastructure, not a workspace integration, as Retell is for voice (modules/voice/retell_api.py) and Stripe for PRD-265. EXPO_PUSH_ACCESS_TOKEN is an environment setting read through config.py, not a key in Settings. httpx is already a dependency: no new Python or npm dependency.

§4.10 'stop and ask first' record (#1254, approved by Gerard 20 Oct): permissions (editors receive the needs_answer push, D16) and tenancy (a device receives only its own workspace's pushes; membership and role are re-checked at send time). No authentication change in this wave beyond W1's device lane.

§4.10 files over AGENTS.md's 800-line limit may NOT grow: core/auth/hybrid.py, api/chat.py, api/approval_grants.py (806), main.py (1,681), services/cli_host_service.py, consumers/chatbot/service.py (3,074), frontend/lib/api-client.ts (3,847+), api/workspaces.py (985), and any other over-800 file the wave touches. The one exception: orchestrator/config.py gains its settings lines; route-manifest.json and config-surface.json gain their entries. W1's api/mobile_devices.py is kept under 400 lines (W1's note): new routes go in the new api/mobile_push.py.

§4.10 code shape on every changed line: functions ≤ 50 code lines, nesting ≤ 4, cyclomatic ≤ 10 (ruff C901), new files 200–400 lines (never over 800), type hints and docstrings on public functions, no mutation of arguments, no swallowed errors; settings only through config.py with each name in reports/config-surface.json (ruff TID251); no hardcoded values.

userStories.description: As the platform, I need one way to hand pushes to Expo and read their receipts, behind an interface, so the fan-out and the receipts job never speak HTTP themselves (PRD-266 §4.4, §4.10 exception 2, US-010).
acceptanceCriteria: New package orchestrator/services/push/ (__init__.py whose docstring names the package's modules and §4.10). services/push/sender.py holds frozen dataclasses PushMessage (to, title, body, data, category_id, channel_id, priority, sound), PushTicket (to, status 'ok' | 'error', ticket_id, error) and PushReceipt (ticket_id, status, error), and the PushSender Protocol: send(messages) -> list[PushTicket] (one ticket per message, in order) and receipts(ticket_ids) -> dict[str, PushReceipt]. No HTTP in this module. → DONE — orchestrator/services/push/__init__.py (docstring names sender, expo, payload, consent, recipients, fanout, receipts, preferences and §4.10), services/push/sender.py (frozen PushMessage — data copied into a read-only mapping — PushTicket, PushReceipt; PushSender Protocol, runtime_checkable, positional-only send/receipts; no HTTP); commit 7c0c14c3b

services/push/expo.py ExpoPushSender implements it: POST to https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send (a module constant) in batches of at most EXPO_SEND_BATCH = 100 messages, and getReceipts at https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/getReceipts in batches of at most EXPO_RECEIPTS_BATCH = 1000 ids; headers Accept and Content-Type application/json and Accept-Encoding gzip, plus Authorization: Bearer <EXPO_PUSH_ACCESS_TOKEN> only when that setting is non-empty; a SYNC httpx.Client (the fan-out and the receipts job run off the event loop: K6), made by a client_factory argument so tests pass httpx.MockTransport; timeout config.EXPO_PUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; TLS verification on. → DONE — services/push/expo.py ExpoPushSender: EXPO_SEND_URL / EXPO_RECEIPTS_URL module constants, EXPO_SEND_BATCH = 100, EXPO_RECEIPTS_BATCH = 1000, BASE_HEADERS (Accept, Content-Type application/json, Accept-Encoding gzip) plus Bearer only when config.EXPO_PUSH_ACCESS_TOKEN is non-empty; sync httpx.Client from a client_factory (default: timeout config.EXPO_PUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, verify=True, follow_redirects=False); tests test_250_messages_are_three_requests_and_250_tickets_in_order, test_the_default_client_verifies_tls_and_times_out_from_config; commit 7c0c14c3b

Expo's answers are validated at the boundary with Pydantic (AGENTS.md: third-party responses): a body that is not JSON, a request-level `errors` array, or a ticket list whose length differs from the batch makes every message of that batch an error ticket ('expo_request_failed'), logged once; a 429 or a 5xx is retried ONCE after EXPO_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0 (a named constant); any other 4xx is not retried. A ticket {status: 'error', details: {error: 'DeviceNotRegistered'}} comes back as PushTicket(status='error', error='DeviceNotRegistered'); a transport error never raises out of send or receipts. → DONE — Pydantic envelopes _SendAnswer/_ReceiptsAnswer: not JSON, request-level errors, wrong shape or a ticket count other than the batch's → every message an expo_request_failed ticket, one warning per batch; 429/5xx retried once after EXPO_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0 (sleep injectable), other 4xx not; DeviceNotRegistered parsed; transport errors (httpx.HTTPError) and data that is not JSON become error tickets, never raised. Code review added: a single ticket not in Expo's shape is expo_malformed_answer for its message only and a malformed receipt is left out (the others kept); error codes fullmatch a plain identifier, else expo_unknown_error; commit 7c0c14c3b

Nothing logs a push token, the access token, a title, a body or data: counts and Expo's error codes only.
